sources.citation: LINGUIST List, MultiTree CLDF dataset (github.com/linguistlist/multitree, branch main): row 'gok_ran,Ranya, rany1238'; rows 568775/790916/852831 'Ranya, Dialect' under Gowli [gok] in trees 14596 (Indo-European: Ethnologue 2005 = Gordon ed. 2005, Ethnologue 15), 19655 (Composite), 21328 (Indo-European: Ethnologue 2009 = Lewis ed. 2009, Ethnologue 16); geography 'India: Madhya Pradesh; Maharashtra, Amravati District.'; sister dialects Lingaayat, Nand, Khamla
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; classification data only. Establishes that 'Ranya' is Ethnologue 15/16's dialect name under Gowli [gok], India, and not the Kurdish town Ranya.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. IX part I: Indo-Aryan family, Central group, Western Hindi and Panjabi, pp. 554-555 ('Gaoli, Raghobansi, and Kirari'; specimen No. 27 'Bundeli (Gaoli), District Chhindwara'). Calcutta.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 554: 'These are the dialects of the castes implied by their names. They are all reported from Chhindwara.. As a matter of fact, they in no way differ from the ordinary broken Bundeli of the district.' i.e. the Gaoli caste 'dialect' is Bundeli (bund1253).

sources.citation: Russell, R. V. & Hira Lal. 1916. The Tribes and Castes of the Central Provinces of India, vol. II, article 'Ahir', pp. 26-27. London: Macmillan.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on language at all. p. 26: 'The Gaolis or milkmen appear to form a distinct branch of the caste with subcastes of their own. Among them are the Nandvans.. the Malwi from Malwa and the Raghuvansi.. The Ranyas take their designation from rān, forest'; p. 27: 'In Betul the weddings of most Gaolis are held in Magh (January), and that of the Ranya subcaste in the bright fortnight of Kartik'. Shows 'Ranya' is a Gaoli subcaste name.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x, languoid gowl1241 "Gowli" [gok] (Bookkeeping, comment_type=Spurious), md.ini with hh_ethnologue_comment
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that Ethnologue E16-E29 list Gowli [gok] (Madhya Pradesh; Maharashtra, Amravati District; Indo-Aryan, Central zone, Western Hindi, Unclassified) and that 'on purely linguistic grounds, both [gok and goj] are spurious, since the Gowli do not have a language that is mutually unintelligible with all surrounding languages' citing Grierson LSI 9:I:554-555 and Russell & Hiralal 'Gowari'.
